# Ten car-following measures on exiD: descriptive statistics

*Generated by `tools/levelx_ssm1d.py exiD`; do not edit by hand. Aggregates only; the data are not redistributed (licence: non-commercial research use). **Descriptive: no outcome (conflict, crash, braking) is used, so nothing here validates or ranks a measure.***

## What was computed

* Data: 93 recordings of exiD; 14,968,717 follower-leader pair-frames with a positive clear gap of at most 200 m; the statistics are on every 25th frame (1 s) of a pair, 599,547 rows.
* Pairs: `precedingId` (highD: the vehicle ahead in the same lane) or `leadId` (exiD, kept only if the leader is ahead and laterally within the follower's width plus 0.5 m). Gap = centre distance along the follower's heading minus half the sum of the lengths; speeds and accelerations (data set values) are projected on that heading; the jerk is the central difference of the acceleration along the consecutive frames of the pair (rows without a neighbouring frame are dropped; the jerk, hence TTC3, is noisy).
* Parameters of the stories, **fixed before the run** (the 2025 paper gives no values; assumptions, not data): reaction time 1 s, leader deceleration 6 m/s2, follower deceleration 6 m/s2. Printed-form differences are as in `docs/ssm1d_notes.md` (the code uses the derived forms). A second set (1.5 s, 4, 4 m/s2) shows the sensitivity.
* Defined values: time measures (TTC1, TTC2, TTC3, TTCD): a positive root within 10 s; DRAC, MDRAC: closing pairs (positive, finite); PSD, MPSD, DCIA: finite; SDI is 0 or 1 for every row. The polygon indicators (TTC, TAdv, T2, TG) use the horizon 10 s with rectangular bodies of the follower's heading and constant velocity.
* The 2025 paper (Future Transportation 5:86, pp. 17-19) names highD among the datasets for the validation it calls the most critical next step and sketches a scenario-based validation against conflict outcomes; this report is the **descriptive first step only** (no outcome).

* Check of the gap: our clear gap minus the data set's own headway column (599,547 rows): median 0.003 m, 5th to 95th percentile -0.086 to 0.054 m, largest absolute 2.147 m.
* Check of the polygon: of 29,541 rows with TTC1 within the horizon, the polygon TTC is defined in 11,379; where both are defined the largest absolute difference is 6.417386 s. TTC1 sees only the distance and the speeds along the heading, the polygon also the lateral separation and the lateral velocities of the bodies, so the two differ where the vehicles move sideways relative to each other or pass side by side (the polygon then has no TTC).
* State of the polygon over all sampled rows: collision course (A) 1.9 %, crossing course (B) 70.7 %, no overlap within the horizon (C) 27.4 %.

## Spearman rank correlation with the polygon indicators

Pairwise complete cases of the defined values (`n` below 200 is not reported). Time measures, TAdv, T2, TG, the lateral margin and beta are larger when safer; DRAC, MDRAC, DCIA, SDI and the required braking are larger when more critical, so expect negative signs between the two families. Descriptive: a high correlation says two readings order the same pairs alike, not that either is right.

Note on the signed margin beta: it uses the prediction-error scales of this data set (`docs/diamond_exiD.md`, tau = 2 s; sigma_delta = 0.0486 s, sigma_eps = 1.2692 m), which are small on straight roads, so beta takes large values; only its ordering is used here.
